First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y-2{y}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3}) \\  & =1-6{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{1-6{y}^{2}}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(1,-1),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(1,-1)} & =\frac{1}{1-6(-1)^{2}}=-\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
